data.title: Thai capital Bangkok declared disaster zone amid flooding
data.description:
Bangkok's governor on Saturday declared Thailand's capital city a disaster-affected zone after residents woke to widespread flooding with some roads inundated, and the prospect of more rain.

Here are some details:

  • Bangkok has experienced more than 24 hours of continuous rainfall, exceeding 150 mm (5.91 inches) in some parts of the city, with the weather agency forecasting thunder storms and heavy to very heavy rain over the weekend

  • Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said the situation "poses a risk to people's lives ... as well as damage to public and private property"

  • The government has issued an emergency advisory for people living near canals to move possessions to higher ground

  • Videos posted on social media showed cars inundated with water and emergency services providing assistance

  • The Bangkok City Administration said it has opened a shelter for evacuees

data.title: Suzuki Planning to Halve Auto Development Time
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: Japan's Suzuki Motor Corporation, the parent of India's largest carmaker Maruti Suzuki, plans to overhaul its manufacturing processes to halve vehicle development time by 2030, enabling it to bring new models to market faster.

Suzuki is targeting improving development efficiency by 30% compared with FY20 levels, while boosting factory productivity by 50% above the standards set at its flagship Manesar plant in Haryana, according to Toshihiro Suzuki, president of Suzuki Motor. "As a challenge to become a company that can keep pace with the speed of change, while halving the new model development period, we will improve development efficiency by 30%, and increase production efficiency by 50%," Suzuki said at the company's Technology Strategy Briefing 2026 on Friday.

The shorter development cycle will change the way Suzuki makes vehicles. Instead of completing planning, design, production engineering, quality and procurement sequentially, these functions will work concurrently from the early stages of a vehicle programme. The company also plans to retain a multi-powertrain strategy and not rely solely on battery electric vehicles, Suzuki said.

He identified Japan and India as the key centres of the company's global business foundation, and said technologies developed in Japan will be shared with Maruti Suzuki India and adapted for individual markets.

India will be strengthened as a manufacturing and export hub, he added. The company is targeting commissioning annual production capacity of 4 million vehicles in India from FY30, up from 2.9 million units now. Output was recently boosted by a fourth production line at Hansalpur, Gujarat, which brought that facility's annual capacity to 1 million units. Maruti Suzuki, which has plants in Gurgaon, Manesar and Kharkhoda, is planning to have a new site in Sanand. Suzuki also plans to deepen digital engineering and expand modularisation, allowing modules to be shared across products and integrating development and manufacturing more closely.

data.title: Snapdeal Parent Bags 189 cr from Anchor Investors
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: AceVector, the parent of ecommerce marketplace Snapdeal, raised 189 crore from anchor investors on September 24, a day ahead of the launch of its initial public offering (IPO), according to a regulatory filing. On its opening day, the IPO got subscribed 23%, with retail investors bidding for 62% of their allocation and non-institutional investors subscribing to 42%.

Domestic investors including Helios Mutual Fund, Singularity Growth and Alchemy Capital participated in the anchor round, picking up shares at 32 apiece. AceVector has set a price band of 30-32 per share for the 420 crore public issue. AceVector is aiming to raise 287 crore in fresh capital, while investors including SoftBank, Nexus Venture Partners and Foxconn are selling shares worth 133 crore through the offer for sale (OFS) component. At the upper end of the price band, the company will get valued at 1,741 crore.

data.title: CCI Seeks More Info on Adani Energy's IntelliSmart Deal
data.description:
Antitrust review of 3,050-cr transaction Twesh Mishra New Delhi: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has sought more information from Adani Energy Solutions on its proposed 3,050-crore acquisition of IntelliSmart Infrastructure. The regulator's website showed the combination's status as "information incomplete" on Thursday evening, two months after the parties filed their notice on July 27.

In a statement announcing the acquisition, Adani Energy Solutions Ltd (AESL) said it was "on track to become India's largest smart metering platform" with a total portfolio of more than 4.7 crore (47 million) smart meters. IntelliSmart is among the top three players in India's smart metering segment, with more than 2.2 crore (22 million) meters across five states, it said.

IntelliSmart is a joint venture between state-controlled National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) and Energy Efficiency Services Ltd (EESL). AESL signed an agreement on June 9 to acquire the company outright, with completion subject to antitrust approval and indicatively expected within 180 days.

Sector watchers said the time taken to respond to regulatory requests does not count towards the CCI's review period. They added that such requests are routine. A summary of the proposed combination said the Adani Group is "primarily involved in the activities of transmission and distribution of electricity and in the business of deployment of advance metering infrastructure for electricity in India".

IntelliSmart, too, is involved in the deployment of advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) for electricity in India, as well as certain smart gas meters. The summary identified "horizontal overlaps" between the two companies in the market for deployment of AMI for electricity in India. It also identified downstream and upstream vertical overlaps in the deployment of meters for piped natural gas (PNG) city gas distribution in India. The provision of cloud services in India was also identified as an upstream relevant market, where the parties have overlaps or linkages.

data.title: India's Equity Indices on a Losing Streak for Seventh Straight Week
data.description:
weighed by surging global yields and oil prices Our Bureau Mumbai: Indian equity benchmarks lost for the seventh straight week, burdened by surging global yields and oil prices, although the gauges eked out modest gains Friday. The Nifty 50 gained 77.40 points, or 0.34%, to close at 23,140.50, while the Sensex rose 315.20 points, or 0.43%, to end at 73,895.74. For the week, the Nifty declined 0.9% and the Sensex fell 0.5%. On BSE, 2,210 stocks advanced and 2,146 declined. Auto and consumer durables stocks gained nearly 0.9% each, while realty rose 0.76% and private banks advanced 0.45%. IT, media, oil and gas and pharma stocks ended lower. In the broader market, the Nifty midcap index slipped 0.15%, while the smallcap index gained 0.02%. India VIX, the market's volatility gauge, declined 4%. "Seven straight weekly losses, and the India VIX still ended the week below 12 and the Nifty is now about 12% below its January record, but this has been a grind, not a rout," said Gaurav Garg, head of research, Lemonn. "It is an orderly de-rating driven by crude above $100, a Federal Reserve that is hiking rather than cutting, and US bond yields at multi-decade highs," he said.

Brent crude hovered around $105.5 a barrel as investors weighed the possibility of a truce between the US and Iran against concerns over increasing attacks on Saudi Arabia by Houthi rebels. A stronger dollar, energy-supply risks, geopolitical uncertainty and sustained foreign institutional selling continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

The rupee closed at 95.8125 against the US dollar, marginally stronger than its previous close of 95.9550. Garg said foreign investors had already pulled more money from Indian equities this year than in all of 2025 despite the June-quarter earnings having beaten estimates. He said a credible agreement between the US and Iran on reopening the Strait of Hormuz could bring down crude prices and trigger short-covering in heavily sold large-cap stocks, particularly banks.

However, insurance and insurance-distribution stocks continue to face a separate regulatory overhang following the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India's (IRDAI) proposed changes on commissions. The proposal has weighed on PB Fintech and other companies in the insurance-distribution segment.

Banks and IT stocks remained among the key weekly drags, falling 1.4% and 2.4%, respectively. On the technical front, the Sensex continued to form bearish candles on the weekly chart, with lower lows for the fourth consecutive week, indicating continued pressure on the broader trend, according to Chandan Taparia, Head of Technical & Derivatives Research at Motilal Financial Services.

data.title: Hotel Cos Put Brakes on Expansion in Gulf amid W Asia Conflict
data.description:
Dilasha Seth & Anumeha Chaturvedi Dubai | New Delhi: Hotel operators are slowing the pace of their Gulf expansion, delaying new openings, pushing back project timelines and becoming more selective about new investments following regional disruption amid West Asia conflict, even as investors continue to assess new opportunities.

Indian Hotels Company (IHCL), which operates the Taj brand, expects some upcoming projects in Saudi Arabia and Bahrain to face delays, but continues to evaluate opportunities in Oman, Abu Dhabi and Dubai, its regional executive told ET. Lemon Tree Hotels exited its Dubai operation a few months ago while Wynn Al Marjan, a multi-billion-dollar casino resort in Ras Al Khaimah, has pushed back its opening to September 2027, with delay adding about $600 million to its projected cost. "I would be lying if I said the crisis would not slow down our expansion plans," said Saurabh Tiwari, vice president-Middle East, Maldives & Sri Lanka, IHCL. "This is a time of survival and being together and supporting our partners." At the beginning of the year, IHCL had been targeting at least 10 operational hotels in the Gulf over the next two to three years, including a property in Saudi Arabia's holy city of Makkah by early 2029, a hotel in Diriyah, near Riyadh, two greenfield hotels under development in Bahrain, and one each in Ras Al Khaimah and Dubai. Currently, it operates three properties in the Gulf region, all in Dubai. Tiwari said there could be a three-six months' delay in some of these projects, noting that Bahrain is also impacted by the conflict.

The company is now looking to open one of its signature restaurants in Bahrain within the next three-six months. "When you cannot change the wind, you change the sail," he said. Chema Basterrechea, global president and COO at Radisson Hotel Group, also said the major Middle East markets have been "heavily impacted." "Saudi Arabia is not as heavily impacted as other neighbouring countries, but the major UAE markets have been severely affected," he said. "We cannot neglect what is happening.

We have more than 50 hotels in the region and many in the pipeline. There can be delays due to the financial commitments and obligations of owners." Experts noted that while hotel project pipelines are expected to remain sizeable, operators are likely to stagger openings as they reassess project economics, demand and the timing of fresh investments. "What we are seeing is a reset in pace, not a retreat from the Gulf," said Akshay Jayaprakasan, associate partner at Redseer Strategy Consultants. "Companies are moving away from chasing footprint and becoming much more selective about the asset, partner and timing. I expect announced pipelines to remain large, but actual openings will probably be more staggered than operators originally envisaged."

data.title: Four Ports Get 'Mega' Status
data.description: Our Bureau New Delhi: The centre has notified four mega ports in the country, a first of its kind nomenclature for the sector. In a gazette notification issued Friday, the ministry of ports, shipping, and waterways listed major ports of Deendayal (Kandla), Jawaharlal Nehru (Nhava Sheva), and Paradip. Adani Group's Mundra Port is the fourth, and only private sector owned asset, in this list. Major ports are governed by the central government. The mega port status will be valid for five years. This is based on a July 30 gazette notification which defined the criteria for this categorisation.

data.title: Snapdeal Parent AceVector Bags 189 cr from Anchor Investors
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: AceVector, the parent of ecommerce marketplace Snapdeal, raised 189 crore from anchor investors on September 24, a day ahead of the launch of its initial public offering (IPO), according to a regulatory filing. On its opening day, the IPO got subscribed 23%, with retail investors bidding for 62% of their allocation and non-institutional investors subscribing to 42%.

Domestic investors including Helios Mutual Fund, Singularity Growth and Alchemy Capital participated in the anchor round, picking up shares at 32 apiece. AceVector has set a price band of 30-32 per share for the 420 crore public issue. AceVector is aiming to raise 287 crore in fresh capital, while investors including SoftBank, Nexus Venture Partners and Foxconn are selling shares worth 133 crore through the offer for sale (OFS) component.

At the upper end of the price band, the company will get valued at 1,741 crore. SoftBank is selling stock worth 88 crore, while retaining shares worth 362 crore at the upper end of the price band. Founders Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal, who together hold around 34% of AceVector directly and through related entities, aren't selling any stake in the IPO. Snapdeal got moved under the AceVector umbrella in 2022.

The parent company also houses ecommerce enablement software firm Unicommerce and house-of-brands company Stellaro Brands. Unicommerce went public in 2024 through a 277 crore IPO. AceVector's operating revenue grew 30% to 510 crore in FY26, while sharply narrowing its net loss to 45 crore from 126 crore in the previous fiscal.

Nearly half of the IPO proceeds will be used for marketing and promotion of Snapdeal, as AceVector seeks to revive the ecommerce marketplace's growth. Snapdeal was once a major rival to Flipkart but has since ceded significant ground. AceVector had filed confidentially for the IPO in July 2025 and received Sebi approval in November. It filed an updated draft prospectus in December.

data.title: Rapido's Ownly Bets on Lower-Cost Food Delivery Model
data.description:
Hyderabad: Rapido's newly launched food delivery business Ownly is seeing an average order value (AOV) of around 250 compared 400-420 at listed rivals Swiggy and Zomato, yet cofounder Aravind Sanka believes it can build a profitable business model around smaller-ticket orders.

Sanka said 85-90% of the cost of running the food-delivery business for existing aggregators is delivery, making logistics the biggest cost for the industry. Ownly is leveraging Rapido's existing technology, teams and logistics network rather than building these capabilities separately to keep costs low. The company is also betting that lower prices can bring new consumers into online food delivery.

According to Sanka, 15% of Ownly's new orders in Bengaluru come from users who had never ordered food online before. The mobility startup, backed by Prosus and WestBridge Capital, on Friday launched Ownly in Hyderabad, its second market after Bengaluru. Ownly has on-boarded 10,000 restaurants in Hyderabad, which it plans to scale up to 30,000.

By the next quarter, Ownly plans to expand across all major metros and tier-1 cities including Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata, Ahmedabad and Surat.

data.title: K'taka, Singapore to Deepen Economic and Investment Ties
data.description:
Our Bureau Bengaluru: Karnataka's industries minister MB Patil held talks with Singapore's minister of state for trade and industry Gan Siow Huang on Friday on strengthening economic and investment cooperation between the two sides.

The discussion was held during Patil's visit to Singapore to attract investments to the state, the industries department said in a statement. Patil said there was considerable scope for deeper collaboration in aerospace and defence, semiconductors, aviation maintenance, repair and overhaul, and other advanced industries.

Further progress would be pursued through the Invest Karnataka Forum and the Singapore Enterprise Centre in Bengaluru, the minister said. CapitaLand Investment is keen to expand its data centre capacity in Karnataka, Patil said in a statement.

The Singapore-headquartered real asset manager is developing a 42 megawatt facility at International Tech Park Bangalore with an investment of about 2,000 crore. Besides, ST Telemedia Global Data Centres (STT GDC) has expressed interest in expanding its presence in the state, he said.

The company operates 34 data centres across 10 cities in India, including three in Bengaluru, with more than 613 MW of IT capacity. STT GDC is investing around 5,000 crore to develop a 100 MW data centre campus on KIADB land in Devanahalli, Patil said. The state government also encouraged TVS Motor Company to increase its investments, he said.

The company, which has a manufacturing presence in Karnataka, was asked to expand in manufacturing, electric mobility, advanced automotive technologies and research and development. Industries department principal secretary Selvakumar and other officials were part of the Karnataka government delegation.

data.title: Trump Warns Xi Against Helping Iran in War, China Assures US it Will Stop Support — But Tehran Says Beijing Promised the Opposite
data.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump pressed Chinese President Xi Jinping during their Washington talks to halt any direct or indirect assistance to Iran, while Tehran said Beijing has assured it that ties with Iran will remain intact.

Trump Pressures Xi Over Iran Support

Trump told Xi that Chinese support for Iran was "totally unacceptable," according to U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue, who discussed the talks with CNBC and Fox News.

Perdue said Washington received assurances from Beijing on Thursday that China would not continue assisting Tehran. He also said the U.S. had already seen some movement on the issue.

The warning comes as Washington examines reports that China has supplied Iran with shoulder-fired air-defense systems and helped Tehran circumvent U.S. sanctions on oil exports, Reuters reported.

Read Also: Trump Taps ‘True Warrior’ Hung Cao As Navy Secretary: Urges Senate To Confirm Him ‘ASAP’

Iran Disputes China’s Commitment to the US

An Iranian senior official, however, told Reuters that Chinese officials had assured Tehran that Beijing would not restrict its economic, political or military relationship with Iran because of pressure from Trump.

Previously, it was reported that Iran was expected to receive Chinese-made shoulder-fired air-defense missile launchers. Tehran has also reportedly used barter-like arrangements to continue selling oil and purchasing Chinese goods despite sanctions.

China Faces Pressure Over Iran Ties

U.S. lawmakers had urged Trump to confront Xi over allegations that Chinese entities provided assistance to Iran that may have contributed to attacks resulting in U.S. casualties.

Trump has previously played down reports that Chinese entities provided satellite imagery to Iran before an attack in Jordan that killed three U.S. troops.

data.title: Lalbaugcha Raja Visarjan 2026: Massive, pink gulal-drenched Ganpati idol reaches Girgaum Chowpatty
data.description:
Mumbai, Sept. 26 -- Mumbai's iconic Lalbaugcha Raja Ganpati idol reached Girgaum Chowpatty on Saturday morning, as thousands of devotees gathered to witness the culmination of the city's 10-day Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations.

The massive pink gulal-drenched idol was carried through packed Mumbai streets on a grand platform, with devotees dancing and accompanying the procession.

The streets came alive as devotees began showering each other with gulal.

The arrival at Girgaum Chowpatty marks a key stage in the final journey of Lalbaugcha Raja, one of Mumbai's most prominent public Ganesh idols.

The idol is eventually immersed in the Arabian Sea at Chowpatty as part of the Ganpati Visarjan rituals.

Reliance Industries Executive Director and Vantara founder Anant Ambani is also expected to participate in the event.

Lalbaugcha Raja is associated with a sarvajanik Ganesh mandal established in 1932 in central Mumbai.

More than nine decades after its establishment, the mandal continues to draw millions of visitors during Ganesh Chaturthi and remains one of the city's most recognised public Ganesh celebrations.

Ganpati Visarjan is observed across India on Anant Chaturdashi. This year it fell on Friday, September 25.

Lalbaugcha Raja's visarjan procession is known for its scale and duration. The idol typically arrives in the early morning hours of the following day of Anant Chaturdashi, often between 6 am and 10 am, with final rituals and immersion taking place in the morning or early afternoon.

In Mumbai and across Maharashtra, elaborate processions bring large numbers of devotees to designated immersion points, where prayers and farewell rituals are performed.

Ganesh Chaturthi 2026 began on September 14, marking the start of the 10-day Ganeshotsav celebrations. The festival is observed across India with the installation of Lord Ganesha idols in homes and public spaces, followed by days of prayers, festive gatherings and offerings.

Devotees traditionally offer flowers, sweets and prayers to Lord Ganesha, with modaks among the offerings associated with the deity.

The celebrations conclude with Ganesh Visarjan, when idols are immersed in water as devotees bid farewell to Ganesha.

data.title: TikTok to Pay $100 Million to Alabama to Settle Child Safety Claims in First-Ever State Deal
data.description:
TikTok has reached a settlement with Alabama over allegations that the platform was designed to addict children and mislead consumers about the safety of its platform.

The state will receive a minimum of $100 million within 45 days and has the potential to get up to $300 million if certain unspecified conditions are met, according to a statement released by the Alabama Attorney General’s office on Friday,

First State Deal Signals a Shift in Strategy

The agreement marks TikTok’s first settlement with a U.S. state, even as it continues fighting similar claims in courts nationwide. Alabama’s case against TikTok was slated to go to trial on Monday. Alabama would have been the first state to bring its claims against TikTok to trial, according to the statement.

“This is a great day for Alabama parents,” Attorney General Steve Marshall said. “TikTok has agreed to give parents real control over what their kids see and how much time they spend on the app.”

The state noted that besides the payment, TikTok must implement several safety features aimed at protecting children using its platform. The features include a two-hour daily time limit, with parental controls.

The deal comes as the regulatory environment continues to change. In July, the Justice Department reversed a federal ban from 2022, allowing employees to reinstall TikTok on government devices. Officials pointed to lower security risks associated with TikTok USDS, a new joint venture in which global investors, including Oracle Corp. , own an 80.1% stake, while Chinese company ByteDance holds the remaining 19.9%.

President Donald Trump chose not to enforce a law passed in April 2024 requiring ByteDance to divest TikTok’s U.S. assets by January 2025 or face a nationwide ban.

TikTok did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment.
